metadata.name: [GCP Compute OTel] Disk performance severely degraded
metadata.description: Alerts when GCE reports a disk's performance status as Severely Degraded for every sample in a 20-minute window. The routine Degraded status is intentionally ignored. Returns one row per affected disk.

data.content:
## Disk performance severely degraded

Compute Engine has reported this disk as **Severely Degraded** for the whole lookback window. Unlike the routine `Degraded` status (background maintenance, usually not noticeable), a persistent Severely Degraded status indicates an infrastructure problem with the underlying storage that affects I/O performance.

### Triage
1. Check disk I/O latency and queue depth for the device. Expect elevated latency without a corresponding increase in IOPS.
2. Check whether other disks in the same zone are affected. A zone-wide pattern points to a GCE storage incident; see the Google Cloud status dashboard.
3. Identify the VM via `instance_id`; `instance_name` is not a dimension of this metric.

### Remediation
If the status persists, open a Google Cloud support case referencing the disk. For critical workloads, fail over to a replica, or snapshot the disk and restore it to a new disk.

### Tuning
The window is 20 minutes and requires at least 3 samples, all Severely Degraded. Shorten the window or switch `MIN` to `MAX` for faster detection. GCP Cloud Monitoring metrics typically arrive several minutes late, so the most recent minutes of the lookback window may be empty; the window is sized to tolerate this.
